articles.title: Node.js Marketplace Webhooks: Rate-Limit Queues, Retries, and Delivery Guarantees
articles.excerpt: Short answer: use a queue-centered design for delayed marketplace webhooks when you need retries and basic rate-limited processing without complex orchestration. Let a scheduler enqueue work, then let…
articles.body: Short answer: use a queue-centered design for delayed marketplace webhooks when you need retries and basic rate-limited processing without complex orchestration. Let a scheduler enqueue work, then let workers control concurrency. Pick a workflow engine when the delivery contract needs durable fan-out, joins, or replay. A marketplace webhook usually starts as an event such as order.paid or shipment.updated . The producer should record the event and enqueue a delivery task. A worker owns the call to the partner API. That boundary keeps the scheduler from becoming a hidden worker pool. Infrai fits this narrow handoff because its queue surface is plain REST: no SDK install, no client-library version to babysit, and any language that can send HTTP can publish work.

articles.title: Refreshing Expired Signed Object Storage Access for Generated SaaS Training Images
articles.excerpt: Short answer: keep generated training images private, store object keys rather than signed links, and have the SaaS API issue a fresh presigned download URL when a preview or download encounters an ex…
articles.body: Short answer: keep generated training images private, store object keys rather than signed links, and have the SaaS API issue a fresh presigned download URL when a preview or download encounters an expired one. Don't turn the bucket public. That doesn't fix the ownership problem, and it isn't an available escape hatch in the evaluated API: public and public-read ACLs are unavailable, so public_url remains null. The least complex design is a private object, a stable database record containing its bucket and key, and a short-lived URL treated as disposable delivery state. For a B2B SaaS team retaining training artifacts, the link is not the artifact. That distinction drives the storage bill, the recovery plan, and the large-file test.

articles.excerpt: Spain publishes the price of every public fuel station as open data. The feed is refreshed every 30 minutes, contains roughly 11,500 stations and needs no API key. That sounded like a good small proje…
articles.body: Spain publishes the price of every public fuel station as open data. The feed is refreshed every 30 minutes, contains roughly 11,500 stations and needs no API key. That sounded like a good small project: download the data, find the cheapest station near a location, and put the result on a map that works on a phone. The result is FuelSpot , a mobile site for comparing stations by fuel and distance. I built it in one day on top of my own small data-web engine. The interesting part was not drawing markers. It was making a public government feed predictable enough to use. The source is simple, with a few sharp edges The source is the Spanish Ministry REST API: GET https://sedeaplicaciones.minetur.gob.es/ServiciosRESTCarburantes/PreciosCarburantes/EstacionesTerrestres/ There is no API key.

articles.title: Understanding IaaS: A Practical Look at AWS EC2
articles.excerpt: Introduction A few years ago, if you wanted to put a website online, you had to buy a physical server, find a place to keep it, and look after it yourself. Today, you can get a server running in minut…
articles.body: Introduction A few years ago, if you wanted to put a website online, you had to buy a physical server, find a place to keep it, and look after it yourself. Today, you can get a server running in minutes, and you only pay for the time you use it. That is the idea behind Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS). As a networking and security student, I wanted to understand how this works in practice. In this article, I explain what IaaS is, what it is made of, and how it looks in real life, using Amazon EC2 as a case study. What is IaaS? IaaS is a cloud computing model where a provider rents out basic computing resources over the internet: virtual machines, storage, and networking. You don't buy or maintain any hardware. You use what you need, when you need it, and pay for what you use.

articles.excerpt: Marketplaces like Amazon, Etsy and most Shopify themes look best when every product sits on a plain white or transparent background. If you only have a phone photo on a kitchen table, here's what actu…
articles.body: Marketplaces like Amazon, Etsy and most Shopify themes look best when every product sits on a plain white or transparent background. If you only have a phone photo on a kitchen table, here's what actually makes the cut-out clean: 1. Shoot for the cut-out, not the scene. Put the item a little away from the wall so it doesn't cast a hard shadow behind it, and use soft daylight from a window. Strong contrast between the product and what's behind it helps any background remover far more than a fancy camera. 2. Keep the original resolution. Don't upscale a small photo before removing the background. Upscaling just invents blurry edges. A 1500–2000 px wide photo is plenty for most store listings. 3. Check the gaps.

articles.title: How to Detect a Leaked API Key From Its Traffic
articles.excerpt: The fastest way to detect a leaked API key isn't a traffic spike. It's the network. A key that has called your API from AWS in Frankfurt for six months doesn't start calling from a residential proxy i…
articles.body: The fastest way to detect a leaked API key isn't a traffic spike. It's the network. A key that has called your API from AWS in Frankfurt for six months doesn't start calling from a residential proxy in Omaha unless somebody else is holding it. Volume alerts won't tell you. Google's threat intelligence team published an LLMjacking report on November 2 describing a threat actor who harvested LLM API keys from public GitHub repos and tested them with single-token requests ( max_tokens=1 ) that stayed under the victims' SIEM volume alerts. By count, that sweep is invisible. By source network, it can show on the first call.

articles.body: On Thursday (Nov. 12), the Euclid space telescope released its first major batch of data, capturing the light of more than a billion objects over an area of sky as big as 9,500 full moons. The data release lays the foundation for one of the largest-ever 3D maps of the cosmos and many groundbreaking discoveries about the nature of dark energy and dark matter. The European Space Agency 's (ESA) Euclid space telescope has been called the "Dark Universe Detective" because of its capability to investigate the dual mysteries of dark matter , the universe's most mysterious stuff, and dark energy , the force accelerating the expansion of the universe. Collectively, these cosmic elements are sometimes referred to as the dark universe.

articles.title: Satellite snaps rare birds-eye view of the ISS | Space photo of the day for Nov. 12, 2026
articles.excerpt: A commercial satellite has spotted the International Space Station, giving us a unique view of the orbiting lab from above.
articles.body: A satellite looks down at the International Space Station in orbit. (Image credit: HEO) A commercial satellite has spotted the International Space Station (ISS), giving us a unique view of the orbiting lab from above. What is it? Most of the time, when we see the ISS, it is from down here on Earth or from the viewpoint of the astronauts onboard, peering out the windows at the station's limbs, solar arrays and instruments. But in this snapshot, which was posted on X on Nov. 9 by the Australian company HEO, we can see the station stretched out in all its glory. HEO specializes in using satellites in low Earth orbit to capture images of other spacecraft, though longer-term the company aims to capture observations far out into the solar system.
articles.author: Chelsea Gohd

articles.title: I used the Vaonis Vespera 3 for weeks and here’s who I would recommend it to — full review
articles.excerpt: I photographed nebulas and star clusters over multiple nights with the Vaonis Vespera 3. It’s one of the most capable smart telescopes I’ve used, but it won’t be for everyone.
articles.body: I’ve spent a lot of time with smart telescopes , from relatively inexpensive Seestar models to the original Vaonis Vespera and the Vespera Pro . They all promise essentially the same thing — you put a telescope outside at night, choose something interesting on your smartphone and let the technology take care of the rest. The Vaonis Vespera 3 does that exceptionally well, but after spending several nights with it, I’m convinced it’s designed for a rather different kind of buyer. The telescope’s optical arm folds into its curved body when switched off. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) At $2,490/£2,199, this is hardly an impulse purchase for the beginner who’s curious about astronomy – you could buy several perfectly capable smart telescopes for the same money.

articles.title: The 'eclipse of the century' will plunge these 8 wonders of the Roman Empire into darkness on Aug. 2, 2027
articles.excerpt: Ancient Roman cities, temples and amphitheaters across the Mediterranean will fall into the moon's shadow during the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027.
articles.body: Ancient Egyptian temples will inevitably dominate the story of the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027 . After all, the path of totality crosses Luxor, home to Karnak, the Valley of the Kings, and some of the ancient world's most famous monuments. But follow the moon 's shadow west and another ancient civilization comes into view. Before reaching Egypt, totality will sweep across the Mediterranean and North Africa, passing over an extraordinary collection of Roman cities, fortresses, theaters, temples and triumphal arches. Many lie within what became Rome's North African provinces, a region that produced some of the empire's wealthiest and most impressive cities.
